overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a meeting through a substantive chair memorandum emailed to all members. No further relief was ordered because the memo was already provided and discussed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee deliberated outside a noticed meeting through a July 2017 chair memorandum sent by email to all members about released executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the memorandum was substantive communication on Committee business and that, therefore, its distribution constituted "deliberation" outside a meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint argued the chair lacked authority to issue the statement on the committee's behalf, the division said that would not be an Open Meeting Law violation.
allegations.key_passage: we note that this allegation, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
